.comment: The attribute policy: every name-set decision the extractor makes about attributes, as data.
This copy is embedded in RazorGraph.Extractor and is the shipped default. A build can point at
an override file (--attribute-policy on the CLI, attributePolicy over MCP) and change any of
these decisions WITHOUT a rebuild - that is the point: policy is configuration, and data is
more flexible than code.
An override file uses this same shape. A section it OMITS is inherited from this default, so a
file that only suppresses one attribute's payload does not have to restate the test frameworks.
A section it INCLUDES replaces that section whole.
testAttributes / lifecycleAttributes / controllerAttributes / bindPropertyAttributes match by
SIMPLE class name including the Attribute suffix (FactAttribute), exactly as the extractor
always has: the attribute may come from any of several assemblies, and the short names do not
collide with anything else in practice. suppressArgumentsFor matches by FULL name as the graph
prints it, with a generic attribute named by its original definition
(Ns.RegisterDependencyAttribute<TInterface>).
Marks a method as a test. Feeds the isTest stamp, coverage seeding, and the rule that test
methods are never entry points.
Setup/teardown hooks for the frameworks that mark them with attributes. xUnit is absent by
design: its hooks are interface members and constructors, recognized in code by shape.
A type carrying one of these is a controller even without a Controller base type.
Marks a property as request-bound; feeds the bindProperty stamp and BindsTo edges.
DecoratedBy edges for these attributes are still emitted, with line and target, but the
args/named/source payload is withheld. unresolvedArgs is NOT suppressible - a build error
must never be configurable into silence. Default empty: uniform emission, so any narrowing
is a visible line in this file rather than a branch in the extractor. The measured candidate
is Xunit.InlineDataAttribute - 1,300 usages in OrchardCore, all of them test case data.
Attributes that mean 'this type is registered with a container', and where to read the
registration from. .NET has no standard registration ATTRIBUTE - the vocabulary is
per-codebase (a RegisterDependencyAttribute<TInterface>, say) - so entries belong in
override files, declared as data and never hardcoded in the extractor.
Shape per entry: 'attribute' is the full name as the graph prints it; 'serviceTypeFrom'
says where the service type is written - 'typeArgument:0', 'argument:0', or
'named:ServiceType'; 'lifetimeFrom' optionally names the argument carrying the lifetime,
e.g. 'named:Lifetime'.
Parsed and carried today so override files can already declare their vocabulary; the
consumer - registration lookup plus the container's own constructor-selection rules - is
the DI work this feeds.
